title: HTML Attributes and Global Attributes
description: Learn about HTML attributes including id, class, title, style, data-* attributes, and event attributes that enhance element functionality and styling.

lessons.title: What are HTML Attributes?
lessons.content: Attributes provide additional information about HTML elements and are always included in the opening tag. They usually come in name/value pairs.

lessons.title: The id Attribute
lessons.content: The id attribute uniquely identifies an element on the page and is often used for styling and scripting.

lessons.title: The class Attribute
lessons.content: The class attribute assigns one or more class names to an element. Classes are used to apply CSS styles to multiple elements and for scripting.

lessons.title: The title Attribute
lessons.content: The title attribute provides additional information about an element, often displayed as a tooltip when hovering over the element.

lessons.title: The style Attribute
lessons.content: This paragraph has inline styles applied.

lessons.title: Global Attributes Overview
lessons.content: Global attributes like id, class, style, title, hidden, and data-* can be added to any HTML element to control behavior and appearance.

lessons.title: Using data-* Attributes
lessons.content: data-* attributes allow you to store custom data on elements that can be accessed via JavaScript.

lessons.title: Event Attributes in HTML
lessons.content: Event attributes like onclick, onmouseover, and oninput enable interaction by triggering JavaScript functions when events occur.

lessons.title: Example: Using id, class, and data-*
lessons.content: Welcome to the site!

lessons.title: Best Practices for Using Attributes
lessons.content: Use id attributes uniquely, apply classes for styling multiple elements, prefer CSS over inline styles, and use data-* for storing custom data.
